questions.text:
Consider the following partial Schedule S involving two transactions T1 and T2. Only the read and the write operations have been shown. The read operation on data item P is denoted by read(P) and the write operation on data item P is denoted by write(P).

Suppose that the transaction T1 fails immediately after time instance 9. Which one of the following statements is correct?
questions.solution:
T2 reads A (time 7) after T1 wrote it (time 2), and T2 commits at time 8 before T1 commits.

When T1 fails, T2 has already committed using a value of A that must be rolled back. Its effects cannot be undone, so S is non-recoverable.

Answer: Schedule S is non-recoverable and cannot ensure transaction atomicity

options: T2 must be aborted and then both T1 and T2 must be re-started to ensure transaction atomicity
Schedule S is non-recoverable and cannot ensure transaction atomicity
Only T2 must be aborted and then re-started to ensure transaction atomicity
Schedule S is recoverable and can ensure atomicity and nothing else needs to be done

questions.text:
If the following system has non-trivial solution,
px+qy+rz=0
qx+ry+pz=0
rx+py+qz=0,
then which one of the following options is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Non-trivial solution needs determinant = 0:

[latex]\begin{vmatrix}p&q&r\\q&r&p\\r&p&q\end{vmatrix}=-(p+q+r)(p^2+q^2+r^2-pq-qr-rp)=0[/latex]

The second factor is [latex]\frac12[(p-q)^2+(q-r)^2+(r-p)^2][/latex], zero only when p = q = r.

Answer: p + q + r = 0 or p = q = r

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

j = 2*3/4 + 2.0/5 + 8/5 = 1 + 0.4 + 1 = 2.4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] j = 2. Then --j makes j = 1, so k = [latex]-[/latex]1.

i + k takes the values [latex]-[/latex]1, 0, 1, 2, 3 (no break, so cases fall through):
- [latex]-[/latex]1, 0: default only [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1 + 1
- 1, 2: case 2, case 3, default [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 + 3
- 3: case 3, default [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2

Total = 10

Answer: 10

questions.text: If for non-zero  [latex]x,af(x)+bf\left ( \frac{1}{x} \right )=\frac{1}{x}-25[/latex] where [latex] a\neq b[/latex]  then [latex] \int_{1}^{2}f(x)dx[/latex] is
questions.solution:
Replace x by 1/x: [latex]af(1/x)+bf(x)=x-25[/latex]. Eliminate f(1/x):

[latex](a^2-b^2)f(x)=\frac ax-25a-bx+25b[/latex]

Integrate from 1 to 2: [latex]a\ln2-25a-\frac{3b}{2}+25b=a(\ln2-25)+\frac{47b}{2}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\frac{1}{a^2-b^2}[a(\ln2-25)+\frac{47b}{2}][/latex]

questions.text: Let G be a connected undirected graph of 100 vertices and 300 edges. The weight of a minimum spanning tree of G is 500. When the weight of each edge of G is increased by five, the weight of a minimum spanning tree becomes ________.
questions.solution:
Every spanning tree has 99 edges, so each tree's weight rises by exactly 99 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 = 495. The same tree stays minimum.

500 + 495 = 995

Answer: 995
